title: Find the Prefix Common Array of Two Arrays
summary: Given two 0-indexed integer permutations A and B of length n, determine an array C where C[i] is the count of elements that appear in both A and B up to index i.
statement: Given two 0-indexed integer permutations A and B of length n, determine an array C where C[i] is the count of elements that appear in both A and B up to index i.
constraints: A and B are permutations of the integers one through n.
For each i, count values appearing in both prefixes A[0:i+1] and B[0:i+1].
Return those n prefix counts in order.
hints: Maintain one seen set for each prefix.
Insert the newly exposed value from A and B at every index.
Append the size of the set intersection.
The sets exactly represent the two prefixes after each insertion, and permutation uniqueness means ordinary intersection size is the required common count.
editorial: The sets exactly represent the two prefixes after each insertion, and permutation uniqueness means ordinary intersection size is the required common count.

tests.explanation: The common prefix-value counts are zero, two, three, and four.
The first prefixes do not intersect, the length-two prefixes share three, and the full prefixes share all three values.
